transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-03 15:00 PST
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Gatekeeper Procurement), Liu (Gatekeeper Security), Marta (Gatekeeper Legal), Devon (Gatekeeper Eng), Samira (Finance)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side — I'm Alex, AE for Redwood Inference, and Priya here is our SE — she'll run the tech part.
[00:14] Jordan: Thanks. Jordan here. we wanted this handoff so procurement and legal can see the flags.
[00:20] Priya: hi all. i'll try to keep the deep tech light for the first half. wanted to confirm the agenda — MSA/DPA redlines, SLA targets, KMS options, and pricing path?
[00:32] Marta: yes that's right, and also any data residency promises. we had a couple of DPA asks in review already.
[00:40] Alex: Great. quick context: gatekeeper is planning a committed Dedicated pool for inference, with a fall-back to our hosted endpoints for burst. we recommended reserved capacity for predictable latency.
[00:54] Devon: small point — our latency target for user-facing features is 150ms p50 and 350ms p95. can Redwood meet that on a mixed LLM workload?
[01:06] Priya: yes, with Dedicated + smaller model variants we can hit p50 in the 80–120ms range for 1–2k token turns; p95 depends on batching and KV cache hit-rate. we'll show you the benchmark plan.
[01:22] Liu: on security — we need clarity on key management. are customer keys in HSM? can we bring our own KMS?
[01:30] Alex: supported. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and on-prem keying in the VPC flow. for Hosted there's an option to integrate with customer KMS via key-wrapping — though egress billing and audit flows differ.
[01:45] Marta: when you say "Private" do you mean the full control plane is customer-managed? we've seen notes calling it "Reedwood Privat" in earlier docs so just making sure—
[01:55] Priya: haha yeah sorry for the typo in the deck — Redwood Private is the VPC/on-prem option, control plane optional. we'll include the architecture diagram in the packet.
[02:08] Jordan: Procurement point: finance is sensitive to any commit. what's your cancellation/leakage policy on reserved capacity?
[02:16] Alex: standard reserved commitment with monthly billing; we can add a ramp schedule and graduated termination windows in the MSA. e.g., 60-day notice for scale-down, prorated credits for unused reserved capacity under defined thresholds.
[02:30] Samira: would like that in writing — also need to see egress fee examples. we run a lot of multi-region inference and egress can surprise us.
[02:40] Priya: sure. we'll attach a sample cost model, including cross-region egress tiers and an example workload. the Optimize toolkit can recommend batching/quantization to reduce units.
[02:52] Devon: on the technical side, we need a preflight for network connectivity: private peering vs VPN, IP allowlists, and whether KV cache persists across instance restarts.
[03:04] Priya: KV cache is ephemeral but can be warm-started; we can walk through cache warming strategies. For connectivity, we support VPC peering and transit gateway attachments; we'll send a checklist.
[03:18] Liu: about audit logs — we require immutable audit trails for 1 year and field-level redaction options for PII. do you have an expose for that?
[03:26] Alex: yes, Redwood Console includes per-route tracing and audit logs; retention tiers are configurable. we'll include retention SLAs and an example of the audit export.
[03:36] Marta: regarding DPA, we marked three clauses for exceptions — subprocessor list, data deletion timelines, and liability caps. Are you able to accept or propose alternatives?
[03:48] Alex: we usually push back on uncapped liabilities; typical approach is to propose a tiered liability cap tied to the annual contract value, and explicit subprocessor listing with at least 30-day notice for changes. we'll send suggested redlines.
[04:03] Jordan: procurement also wants to understand the SLA credits formula. if p95 latency misses for a quarter, how do credits apply?
[04:12] Priya: in our standard SLA we offer credits as percentage of monthly invoice for missed SLOs, scaled by severity. For dedicated pools we can tighten p95 targets and adjust the credit schedule. we'll drop the math into the SLA appendix.
[04:26] Devon: i want to flag a scenario: heavy embedding workloads push memory pressure — will you auto-fallback to a smaller model? there's concern about output quality vs cost.
[04:36] Priya: good question. we support smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants. we also have a quality monitoring hook so you can set regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
[04:48] Liu: one more KMS question — if we bring our own HSM, can Redwood perform model compilation and kernel selection without accessing keys? how's the signing flow?
[04:59] Priya: compile happens at runtime on infer nodes; data-at-rest keys stay in customer-managed HSM. signing flows can be done via key-wrap where Redwood never sees plaintext keys; we can share a diagram but there are some engineering steps.
[05:14] Alex: want to cover timelines — gatekeeper's ask was to get procurement greenlight by mid-March. are those stakeholders aligned?
[05:22] Jordan: yes procurement wants final pricing and redlines by 3/10 if possible.
[05:27] Marta: legal needs 72 hours to review redlines once received.
[05:31] Alex: good. so action: i'll send the MSA/DPA redline packet today, plus a dedicated SLA appendix and KMS integration guide. Priya will set the benchmark window.
[05:42] Samira: FYI finance will want an option for a pilot commit (90 days) before full annual reservation. is that supported?
[05:50] Alex: yes we can propose a pilot-commit path with a capped usage band and conversion credit on full commit. we'll draft that in the pricing sheet.
[05:58] Jordan: any competitors we should affirm you're differentiated from from a procurement perspective?
[06:04] Alex: folks typically compare us to BigCloud AI or NimbusServe; differentiation is our production-first runtime, unified deployment modes, and cost controls like smart batching and caching.
[06:14] Marta: will you also send SOC2 and ISO cert PDFs? we need copies for security intake.
[06:20] Alex: yes — sending the compliance pack with cert PDFs and our SOC2 report extract.
[06:27] Devon: quick tech note — when Priya runs the benchmark, can you run a mixed-load test: 60% generation, 40% embeddings, with 1k token contexts?
[06:36] Priya: Yup that's exactly the plan, we'll include both p50/p95 and 99th tail for token latency, plus token-cost burn rates.
[06:44] Jordan: outstanding. i think this is enough to move to procurement queue once we have papers and the pricing spreadsheet.
[06:52] Alex: ok wrapping up — recap of next steps and owners, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark window and a secure share link for the redlines. anything else?
[07:03] Liu: please highlight network segmentation and encrypted-in-transit diagrams in the pack.
[07:08] Alex: will do. thanks everyone.
[07:12] Marta: thanks, bye.

Notes: occasional ASR quirks in transcript: "Reedwood" instead of Redwood, "KV cash" vs KV cache in one line. There were brief cross-talk moments.
